title: Agrasen ki Baoli Delhi – History, Timings & Mystery
content:
Agrasen ki Baoli - Delhi’s Stepwell of History & Mystery,

Agrasen ki Baoli in Delhi is a centuries-old stepwell that blends history, architecture, and legend. Hidden among Connaught Place’s busy streets, this monument is both a peaceful escape and one of Delhi’s most fascinating attractions.

The Story Behind Agrasen ki Baoli

The exact origins of Agrasen ki Baoli remain a mystery. Some believe it was built by the legendary king Maharaja Agrasen during the Mahabharata era and later rebuilt in the 14th century by the Agarwal community. Today, it stands as one of the most unique stepwells in India.

Architecture & Design

Agrasen ki Baoli is 60 meters long and 15 meters wide, with over 100 stone steps leading down to the water level. The arched corridors, carved niches, and symmetrical design showcase early Indian architecture. While the stepwell is now dry, it once provided water to the city and served as a community gathering place.

Legends & Mysteries

Many locals believe the baoli is haunted, with stories that the waters once lured people into its depths. While these tales add a sense of mystery, most visitors find the place calm, photogenic, and full of character.

What to Expect When You Visit

Today, Agrasen ki Baoli is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). It has become a popular spot for travelers, photographers, and even Bollywood shoots (it appeared in movies like PK). The peaceful atmosphere makes it perfect for exploring history right in the heart of modern Delhi.

Best Time to Visit: October to March for pleasant weather. Early mornings or late afternoons give the best light for photography.

How to Reach:

  • By Metro: Nearest metro station is Barakhamba Road (Blue Line), about a 10-minute walk.
  • By Bus/Auto: Well-connected via DTC buses and autos from anywhere in central Delhi.
  • By Car: Street parking in Connaught Place is available but can be limited during office hours.

Entry Fee: 

No Entry fee, Free for all visitors.

Travel Tip: Wear sturdy shoes-the uneven stone steps can be slippery, especially after rain.
excerpt: Agrasen ki Baoli in Delhi is an ancient stepwell with over 100 stone steps, unique architecture, and mysterious legends. Located near Connaught Place, it’s free to visit and a must-see for history lovers, photographers, and curious travelers.
